it0_no_feature_paths: Baseline before any coverage-specific post-processing: hard feature constraints in the field + proximity snapping of vertices to creases (the default before edge-path recovery). Reproduced with the current code by disabling path recovery (QRM_NO_FEATURE_PATHS=1).
it1_feature_paths: Hypothesis: many creases have an edge loop running next to them (offset by a fraction of an element) but not on them.

Change: edge-path recovery - for every crease chain, a directed-edge Dijkstra through the quad mesh (cost: distance to the crease, misalignment, turning inside a face), the path is snapped onto the crease with a monotone arclength map and locked during relaxation; short chains get jointly chosen endpoints.
Cost: none by construction (no topology change). Current default.
it2_feature_refine: Hypothesis: creases closer than one element need more vertices locally.
Change: refine (1->4 with conforming hanging-node templates) the quads around every chain without a path, then trace again; two rounds.
Observed trade-off: template triangles lower the quad ratio and the transition fronts add irregular vertices; the face count grows. Kept as opt-in (--feature-refine 2).
it3_loops_extra_faces: Hypothesis: a crease that runs lengthwise along a quad strip can get its own edge loop by splitting that strip lengthwise (pure quads, no new irregular vertices).

Change: for each chain without a path, find the longest run of quads it crosses rung-to-rung and split the whole strip (through the crease inside the run, on the midline elsewhere); self-crossing strips split their crossing faces into 4. No face-count control in this run (--no-face-match).
Observed: whole strips are 10-60x longer than the crease runs, so most added faces do not help coverage.
it4_loops_equal_faces: Same as it3 but with face-count control: if the output exceeds 1.08x the target, the field is re-solved at a proportionally lower budget so the output lands on the target face count.
Purpose: fair comparison at equal face count.
it5_partial_loops: Hypothesis: splitting only the crease's own run (plus up to 8 faces when that reaches the strip's end) gives the same local loop at a fraction of the face cost; each open end leaves one hanging vertex, resolved as quad + triangle, and adjacent triangles are re-paired.

Guards: runs shorter than 3 faces are skipped; loop insertion stops at 0.6 x triangle budget (triangle budget = 1.2 % of the target faces), so the quad ratio cannot drop below ~98.8 % from this step. Face-count control on.
it6_partial_loops_curved_splits: Hypothesis: on tightly curved creases the path vertices are on the crease but the straight edges between them are not (chord sag > 0.1 L or turn > 25 deg).

Change: split every recovered path edge whose chord midpoint is > 0.09 L from the crease or whose direction deviates > 23 deg, at the crease point; the two adjacent quads become quad + triangle. Worst deviations first, within the remaining triangle budget; two passes.
it7_hybrid_sb10: Hybrid, per crease: partial edge loops for long creases without a path, one round of local refinement only around short creases (<= 8 L), curved-crease splits.

Every operation is applied tentatively and kept only if the mesh stays within a triangle budget (+1.5 % of target faces) and a singularity budget (+10 irregular vertices per 1k target faces); checks are topological, so this is cheap.
Face-count control re-solves only above 1.10x the target (Instant Meshes itself lands at 0.84-1.03x).
it8_hybrid_sb25: Same as it7 with a singularity budget of +25 per 1k target faces: measures the coverage / singularity trade-off.
it9_trace_all: Hypothesis: on inputs whose crease network is denser than the resolution, the field gets a reduced crease set (to keep the integer solve stable), so path recovery never sees the remaining creases. Change: path recovery uses the full crease set while the field keeps the reduced one. Vertex moves only - no topology change.
it10_coverage_mode: it8 (hybrid, singularity budget 25) + full-set path recovery (it9).
code_note: it0-it8 ran on the working tree between commits f0a388b and the commit that adds this note; it5/it6 used an earlier triangle budget (1.2 %, loops limited to 0.6 of it) and face-count threshold (1.08x). From it9 on, each run's meta.json records the exact commit.
